source_note: Thariq's tip (interview me with questions, write a spec, then build it in a new session); Anthropic's best practices also suggest letting Claude interview you. Planned as an interactive day with Sebi answering from a fixed sheet whose rule is: only facts already in the task text, otherwise 'No preference, your call.' Run automated instead (Sebi's decision, 21 Sep): a headless run can't show the AskUserQuestion picker, so step 1 asks the agent to list all its questions in one message; step 2 resumes the session with one fixed reply that applies the sheet's rule to every question and asks for SPEC.md; step 3 is a fresh session in the same repo copy: 'Implement SPEC.md. Run its verification step before you finish.' The answers add no facts beyond the task text, by design, as the sheet required. Without: the standard single call. Time, cost, turns and tokens summed over all steps; the 20-minute cap covers all of them.

with.label: Interview, answers from the sheet, SPEC.md, fresh build
with.prompt_prefix: Before changing any code, interview me in detail about anything in this task that is unclear. Ask all your questions in one message, as a numbered list, with options where it helps. Then stop and wait for my answers.

turns.prompt: Here are my answers to all your questions: use only what the task text says. For anything it does not say: no preference, your call. Now write the complete spec to SPEC.md and stop. Don't change any code.
Implement SPEC.md. Run its verification step before you finish.
